text: Купянское направление После приезда временно исполняющего обязанности главкома ВСУ из-за боевых неудач и бездействия на всех направлениях, хохляцкое ЦИПСО получили больших «люлей». Этим гениальным людям не пришло в голову ничего, кроме как сделать очередной громкий информационный вброс о занятии бравыми и смелыми солдатами ВСУ населенного пункта Двуречное . Проснувшись после очередного передоза, решили пририсовать себе кусок в 14 кв. км, лишь бы свинячья рожа начальника была довольна. Обстановка на самом деле обстоит так. 350-й мотострелковый полк, который стоит на этом направлении, уверенно наступает и пресекает жалкие попытки противника малыми группами зайти и закрепиться у реки Оскол. Наши операторы дронов наблюдают, как дезориентированные и деморализованные солдаты и наемники ВСУ предпринимают убогие попытки прорваться к реке Оскол, но так как даже их командиры плохо знают местность и просто отправляют личный состав на убой, наши подразделения, как в тире, отстреливают боевиков, прущих с визгом, не понимая, куда и что им нужно делать. Гнилая натура противника выдала очередной «шедевр» своих успехов на картинке, выдавая желаемое за действительное, лишь бы верхушка была довольна,
author: Boris Rozhin

text: Пользователи Apple начали что-то подозревать. ВЦИОМ : 51% пользователей смартфонов не стали бы рассматривать iPhone при следующей покупке Более половины опрошенных пользователей смартфонов (51%) не стали бы рассматривать iPhone при следующей покупке из-за ограниченной доступности приложений в App Store. О недоверии к Apple в связи с удалением российских приложений сообщил каждый второй российский пользователь смартфонов, еще 45% полагают, что ограничения могут подтолкнуть россиян к переходу на Android. Данные приводятся в исследовании ВЦИОМ. Последствия ограничений заметнее среди владельцев iPhone. Об удалении приложений как о затронувшей их проблеме заявили 69% пользователей устройств Apple против 37% владельцев смартфонов на Android. Ситуация беспокоит 56% владельцев iPhone и 29% пользователей Android. У 64% опрошенных владельцев iPhone перестали приходить уведомления, 46% столкнулись с отсутствием обновлений, 42% не смогли скачать нужное приложение. Еще 39% сообщили, что не могли вовремя получить сообщение или ответить на него. Пользоваться смартфоном стало менее удобно для каждого второго владельца iPhone и четверти пользователей Android. text: В Киеве готовят списки граждан, которым потребуется эвакуация из-за длительного отсутствия тепла и света предстоящей зимой. Об этом заявили в киевской администрации. Жители Киева и других городов-миллионников должны решить, готовы ли они жить без воды и света в отопительный сезон, - нардеп Украины от "Слуги народа" Богдан Кицак. Зимой украинцы могут сидеть без света по 14–15 часов в сутки. Самая сложная ситуация ожидается в Одессе, Харькове, Кривом Роге, Днепре и Запорожье, — энергетический эксперт Юрий Корольчук

text: Правительство Германии одобрило законопроект о реформировании спецслужб страны, предполагающий значительное расширение полномочий Федерального ведомства по охране конституции, которое выполняет функции контрразведки, и Федеральной разведывательной службы, сообщило агентство DPA. Разведслужба, отвечающая за внешнюю разведку, теперь сможет воздействовать на ИТ-инфраструктуру иностранной державы во время продолжающейся кибер- или дезинформационной атаки на Германию. Сотрудники Федерального ведомства по охране конституции смогут проникать в жилые помещения, чтобы заменять компоненты взрывчатых веществ на безвредный порошок.
author: Boris Rozhin

text: Западноевропейские псы истошно лают про так называемый российский теневой флот. Давайте разберёмся, о чём это? Под ним подразумеваются обычные торговые суда, которые ходят под нероссийским флагом, но выполняют перевозки в наших интересах. Подобный флаг обычно называют «удобным», или «благоприятным». Это такая система, где судно регистрируется в стране, отличной от страны владельца, ради экономии на налогах и регулировании. К ним относятся Панама, Либерия, Маршалловы Острова, Багамы, Белиз, Бермуды, Каймановы Острова, Кипр, Мальта, Сейшелы. Конечно, никаких прав у европейских собак задерживать такие суда ни в соответствии с Конвенцией по международному морскому праву 1982 года, ни в соответствии с национальным законодательством нет. Это чистой воды произвол. Но отсюда вытекает один важный вывод: абсолютное большинство западноевропейских судов также ходят под удобными флагами. А значит что? Значит, руководствуясь симметричным подходом (что справедливо), Россия вправе атаковать любое торговое судно вражеских стран, находящееся как в наших, так и в нейтральных водах при наличии достаточных подозрений, что оно перевозит груз в интересах противника. То есть любой груз! И таких судов очен
author: Boris Rozhin

text: Британия хочет возобновить военные контакты с РФ на высоком уровне, британские военачальники опасаются риска "непреднамеренной эскалации" из-за отсутствия диалога, пишет The Times. Вопрос о необходимости возобновления диалога был поставлен из-за упредительной стрельбы российского фрегата "Адмирал Григорович" в июне в Ла-Манше в связи с опасным приближением яхты под британским флагом. В последний раз начальник Генштаба ВС РФ Герасимов общался с начальником штаба обороны ВС Великобритании в сентябре 2022 года.

text: Группировка войск "Север" освободила село Водяное Харьковской области! Штурмовые подразделения 11 тп ГВ "Север" в ходе ожесточенных боев выбили националистов 129 отмбр из села Водяное Ольховатской сельской общины и освободили населенный пункт. В районе Водяного отмечено избирательное действие заградительных отрядов ВСУ, которые дали бежать бывшим заключенным из состава 129 отмбр , но убили нескольких солдат из подразделения обеспечения, которые также пытались покинуть позиции. С высокой долей вероятности, в заградотрядах ВСУ также действуют вчерашние уголовные преступники. Населенный пункт был освобожден в ходе решительных действий наших штурмовых отрядов, которые за несколько суток смогли прорваться через лесополосы и разгромить превосходящие силы противника. Эти успешные действия Северян позволяют не только освободить очередной населенный пункт исконно русской Харьковской области, но и подойти к окраинам крупного логистического центра ВСУ на данном участке фронта - села Ольховатка. @warriorofnorth

text: Обстановка в зоне ответственности группировки войск "Восток" за прошедшие сутки В полосе ответственности вскрыты и уничтожены две диверсионно-разведывательные группы противника. Сорвано 11 контратак ВСУ. До рубежей спешивания уничтожены БТР, 3 бронемашины, 21 единица автомобильной, а также до двух взводов живой силы ВСУ. На северном участке воины-забайкальцы прорвали оборону противника и освободили Новое Поле Запорожской области, установив контроль над крупным районом обороны противника. Кроме того, ударными БпЛА и артиллерией нанесены удары по позициям ВСУ в Зоревке и Рыбальском, а также в районе Коломийцев, Подговориловки и Великомихайловки. Северо-западнее Зарницы воины из Бурятии продолжили вклинение в глубину обороны ВСУ, а также пресекли ротацию, уничтожив технику и ПВД противника в районе Барвиновки и Воскресенки. Западнее Лесного сахалинские воины поразили места скопления противника в Никольском, Новосолошино и Тимошовке. В результате комплексного огневого поражения уничтожено свыше трех взводов противника. Западнее Ровного и Копани воины-приморцы вклинились в оборону противника и продвинулись в направлении Широкого, уничтожив свыше 15 пунктов управления БпЛА и свыше 30 ант

text: Пекин усиливает позиции в Западной Африке: Кот-д’Ивуар получил китайские дроны Кот-д’Ивуар подтвердил получение как минимум двух китайских ударно-разведывательных БЛА Wing Loong II . Появление этих машин стало первым публичным свидетельством реализации крупного китайско-ивуарийского контракта, заключённого в июне 2024 года . Тогда Минобороны Кот-д’Ивуара сообщило о соглашении с AVIC на поставку авиационной техники, однако конкретные типы и количество машин официально не раскрывались. Теперь стало известно, что в пакет поставок вошли Wing Loong II . Для Абиджана это серьёзное усиление возможностей воздушной разведки и нанесения ударов. Поставка проходит на фоне масштабной модернизации вооружённых сил Кот-д’Ивуара. В 2025 году правительство выделило на оборону и безопасность примерно $2 млрд , что стало одним из крупных военных бюджетов в истории страны. Абиджан одновременно расширяет парк техники сразу по нескольким направлениям. На вооружение поступают южноафриканские M36 Puma и SD Rooikat , китайские WZ-551, VN-22B , EQ2050 , турецкие Cobra II , а также бронемашины Shrek эмиратской компании Streit Group. На море Кот-д’Ивуар располагает израильским патрульным кораблём OPV-45 Espoir

text: Tyumen Region Imposes Mass Pig Culls Over Mystery Outbreak Aug. 12, 2026 72.ru Authorities in western Siberia’s Tyumen region have begun forcibly seizing and culling domestic pigs across several rural villages following an outbreak of an undisclosed disease, the local outlet 72.ru reported Wednesday. As part of quarantine measures imposed Friday, disinfection checkpoints manned by police have reportedly been set up along Golyshmanovsky District roads to spray passing vehicles and prevent pork products from leaving the area. Video shared by the outlet showed men in hazmat suits spraying vehicles and photographs of them inspecting pigsties. Local veterinary officials reportedly refused to name the pathogen publicly, saying access to the information is restricted, while residents claimed it is being referred to as an “extraordinarily dangerous disease.” According to 72.ru, local agricultural experts believe the outbreak is likely African swine fever, a viral disease with a nearly 100% mortality rate among pigs but harmless to humans. From June to July, ad tracking firm Digital Budget said spending on direct banner ads on Wildberries plummeted 63%. title: 3 Killed, 2 Grain Terminals Halt Work in Novorossiysk After Ukrainian Attack, Sources Say
text: 3 Killed, 2 Grain Terminals Halt Work in Novorossiysk After Ukrainian Attack, Sources Say By Reuters Aug. 12, 2026 @exilenova_plus / Telegram Ukraine hammered Russia's Black Sea port city of Novorossiysk in a massive overnight drone attack that put two major grain terminals out of action, according to Russian industry sources, raising fears in global markets of a disruption to supplies. Russia is the world's largest wheat exporter and most of those exports are shipped via its Black Sea ports like Novorossiysk. title: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App
text: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App Aug. 12, 2026 pay.yandex.ru Major Russian digital wallet and payment service Yandex Pay said Wednesday that its application had been removed from Apple’s App Store. The removal means iPhone users in Russia can no longer download or update Yandex Pay. The app allows users to store cards, make contactless payments and split purchases across Yandex’s suite of services. In a statement, Yandex Pay assured customers that their money remained secure and that the app would continue to function for users who already had it installed. “Most importantly, don’t delete the app,” Yandex Pay said, urging users to turn off automatic updates and use its web-based version within mobile browsers instead. “We’re sad this happened too… We’ll figure something out with the app,” Yandex Pay said. Apple has not publicly commented on the removal, though it has delisted apps linked to sanctioned Russian entities in recent months. While Yandex Pay has not itself been targeted directly by Western sanctions, Yandex Bank was sanctioned by the United Kingdom in June. Yandex Pay is still available for Android users on Google Play. text: Russia Forced to Import Gasoline From India Amid Domestic Shortages Aug. 12, 2026 Smoke rising above an oil refinery in Moscow following a Ukrainian strike. Social media via REUTERS Russia last week received its first shipment of gasoline from India to offset domestic fuel shortages caused by Ukrainian drone strikes on its oil refineries, Bloomberg reported Wednesday, citing ship tracking data. According to market analytics firm Kpler, the Indian gasoline arrived at a Russian port on Wednesday, Aug. 5. It was reportedly produced by Nayara Energy, an Indian refiner partially owned by Russian state oil giant Rosneft. Russian-flagged tanker Cyclone in mid-June reportedly loaded 42,000 metric tons of gasoline from the Vadinar refinery in western India and used a chain of shadow fleet tankers off the coast of Egypt. title: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App
text: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App Aug. 12, 2026 pay.yandex.ru Major Russian digital wallet and payment service Yandex Pay said Wednesday that its application had been removed from Apple’s App Store. The removal means iPhone users in Russia can no longer download or update Yandex Pay. The app allows users to store cards, make contactless payments and split purchases across Yandex’s suite of services. In a statement, Yandex Pay assured customers that their money remained secure and that the app would continue to function for users who already had it installed. “Most importantly, don’t delete the app,” Yandex Pay said, urging users to turn off automatic updates and use its web-based version within mobile browsers instead. “We’re sad this happened too… We’ll figure something out with the app,” Yandex Pay said. Apple has not publicly commented on the removal, though it has delisted apps linked to sanctioned Russian entities in recent months. While Yandex Pay has not itself been targeted directly by Western sanctions, Yandex Bank was sanctioned by the United Kingdom in June. Yandex Pay is still available for Android users on Google Play. title: The Economist: Ramzan Kadyrov says his republic has sent 70,000 men to fight in Ukraine, but Chechens make up just 0.2% of Russia’s confirmed war dead
text: Ramzan Kadyrov and Vladimir Putin at a meeting with Chechen special forces in Gudermes. August 2024 Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov regularly voices support for Russia’s war against Ukraine, but Chechnya’s authorities do not actually share the Kremlin’s interests in that war, The Economist reports . “Whatever interests Moscow has in Ukraine, we are a world apart from them,” said an anonymous source whom The Economist described as “a well-known Chechen with close ties to the leadership.” The source said Kadyrov “understands the situation perfectly well” and has no desire to sacrifice his people for the sake of the “Russian world.” Kadyrov said in April that Chechnya had sent more than 70,000 fighters to the front, the equivalent of 9% of the republic’s male population. title: Russia Forced to Import Gasoline From India Amid Domestic Shortages
text: Russia Forced to Import Gasoline From India Amid Domestic Shortages Aug. 12, 2026 Smoke rising above an oil refinery in Moscow following a Ukrainian strike. Social media via REUTERS Russia last week received its first shipment of gasoline from India to offset domestic fuel shortages caused by Ukrainian drone strikes on its oil refineries, Bloomberg reported Wednesday, citing ship tracking data. According to market analytics firm Kpler, the Indian gasoline arrived at a Russian port on Wednesday, Aug. 5. It was reportedly produced by Nayara Energy, an Indian refiner partially owned by Russian state oil giant Rosneft. Russian-flagged tanker Cyclone in mid-June reportedly loaded 42,000 metric tons of gasoline from the Vadinar refinery in western India and used a chain of shadow fleet tankers off the coast of Egypt. Last month, Reuters reported that Russia had quietly begun purchasing gasoline from Indian refineries to stabilize domestic supplies. Russian officials have since claimed the domestic fuel market partially stabilized. title: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App
text: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App Aug. 12, 2026 pay.yandex.ru Major Russian digital wallet and payment service Yandex Pay said Wednesday that its application had been removed from Apple’s App Store. The removal means iPhone users in Russia can no longer download or update Yandex Pay. The app allows users to store cards, make contactless payments and split purchases across Yandex’s suite of services. In a statement, Yandex Pay assured customers that their money remained secure and that the app would continue to function for users who already had it installed. “Most importantly, don’t delete the app,” Yandex Pay said, urging users to turn off automatic updates and use its web-based version within mobile browsers instead. “We’re sad this happened too… We’ll figure something out with the app,” Yandex Pay said. Apple has not publicly commented on the removal, though it has delisted apps linked to sanctioned Russian entities in recent months. While Yandex Pay has not itself been targeted directly by Western sanctions, Yandex Bank was sanctioned by the United Kingdom in June. Yandex Pay is still available for Android users on Google Play. title: Tyumen Region Imposes Mass Pig Culls Over Mystery Outbreak
text: Tyumen Region Imposes Mass Pig Culls Over Mystery Outbreak Aug. 12, 2026 72.ru Authorities in western Siberia’s Tyumen region have begun forcibly seizing and culling domestic pigs across several rural villages following an outbreak of an undisclosed disease, the local outlet 72.ru reported Wednesday. As part of quarantine measures imposed Friday, disinfection checkpoints manned by police have reportedly been set up along Golyshmanovsky District roads to spray passing vehicles and prevent pork products from leaving the area. Video shared by the outlet showed men in hazmat suits spraying vehicles and photographs of them inspecting pigsties. title: St. Petersburg Philosophy Professor Detained Over $40 ‘Extremist’ Navalny Donations
text: St. Petersburg Philosophy Professor Detained Over $40 ‘Extremist’ Navalny Donations Aug. 12, 2026 Igor Zaytsev. aquaviva.ru St. Petersburg police have detained a prominent philosophy professor for allegedly donating 3,500 rubles ($42) to groups affiliated with the late opposition activist Alexei Navalny. St. Petersburg police said it cooperated with the Federal Security Service (FSB) to detain a 58-year-old local resident as part of a criminal case into financing extremist activity that was opened on July 31. While the police withheld his name, several media outlets identified the man as Igor Zaytsev, 58, an associate professor and deputy dean of the faculty of philosophy and theology at the Dostoevsky Russian Christian Humanities Academy. In a video released by the police, law enforcement officers were heard asking Zaytsev about his electronic devices before carrying out extensive searches in his home. “I personally supported Alexei Navalny,” Zaytsev told the officers on camera. title: Orenburg Region Imposes Fuel Rationing After Ukrainian Refinery Attack
text: Orenburg Region Imposes Fuel Rationing After Ukrainian Refinery Attack Aug. 12, 2026 Ural56.ru Russia’s Orenburg region near the border with Kazakhstan has introduced fuel rationing and an odd-even license plate system at gas stations, following a Ukrainian drone attack on a local oil refinery. “I’ll be honest, our region is facing a difficult fuel situation. The enemy’s latest terrorist act has created certain problems,” Orenburg region Governor Yevgeny Solntsev said Wednesday. The Ukrainian military said Tuesday it had attacked the Orsknefteorgsintez refinery, located around 1,500 kilometers (930 miles) from the border with Ukraine. The refinery has an annual processing capacity of 6.6 million metric tons. Under the new restrictions, drivers with license plates ending in even numbers are limited to fuel purchases on even days, while those with license plates ending in odd numbers are limited to fuel purchases on odd days. Authorities have also capped individual fuel purchases at 30 liters (8 gallons) of gasoline per customer and banned sales into portable containers. title: Putin Threatens Retaliation if Europe Seizes Russian Ships
text: Putin Threatens Retaliation if Europe Seizes Russian Ships Aug. 12, 2026 President Vladimir Putin visits the Russian Navy missile cruiser Varyag. kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin said Moscow would retaliate in kind if European countries carried out plans to seize Russian commercial vessels, describing the proposed measures as “piracy and robbery.” “We see the authorities of certain countries attempting, in violation of international maritime law, to restrict the movement of vessels operated by our businesses,” Putin said during a meeting with Pacific Fleet personnel aboard the missile cruiser Varyag on Wednesday. “And recently, they went so far as to consider seizing our vessels and selling the property they have plundered from us. This is, of course, nothing other than piracy and robbery.” The warning follows the European Union’s adoption in July of a mechanism allowing member states to confiscate and sell Russian oil carried aboard shadow fleet vessels attempting to evade the bloc’s sanctions. title: Chinese EV makers move factories to Africa as global trade shifts | AP News
text: Workers assemble the Zeekr 001 EV models at the Chinese automaker Zeekr assembly plant in Ningbo, east China’s Zhejiang Province, April 17, 2025. (AP Photo/Andy Wong, File) By ALLAN OLINGO Leer en español Add AP News on Google Add AP News as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Share Share Facebook Copy Link copied Print Email X LinkedIn Bluesky Flipboard Pinterest Reddit NAIROBI, Kenya (AP) — Chinese automakers are increasingly shifting from exporting vehicles to building them in Africa, betting that rapid urbanization, a growing middle class and supportive government policies will make the continent one of the industry’s last major growth markets. It’s part of a strategy for coping with slowing demand at home and rising trade barriers in Europe and North America. Analysts say the shift could reshape Africa’s automotive industry by creating jobs, developing local supply chains and accelerating adoption of electric vehicles, although weak infrastructure and policy uncertainty remain significant obstacles. The Ukrainian military said Tuesday it had attacked the Orsknefteorgsintez refinery, located around 1,500 kilometers (930 miles) from the border with Ukraine. The refinery has an annual processing capacity of 6.6 million metric tons. Authorities have also capped individual fuel purchases at 30 liters (8 gallons) of gasoline per customer and banned sales into portable containers. title: Putin Threatens Retaliation if Europe Seizes Russian Ships
text: Putin Threatens Retaliation if Europe Seizes Russian Ships Aug. 12, 2026 President Vladimir Putin visits the Russian Navy missile cruiser Varyag. kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin said Moscow would retaliate in kind if European countries carried out plans to seize Russian commercial vessels, describing the proposed measures as “piracy and robbery.” “We see the authorities of certain countries attempting, in violation of international maritime law, to restrict the movement of vessels operated by our businesses,” Putin said during a meeting with Pacific Fleet personnel aboard the missile cruiser Varyag on Wednesday. “And recently, they went so far as to consider seizing our vessels and selling the property they have plundered from us. This is, of course, nothing other than piracy and robbery.” The warning follows the European Union’s adoption in July of a mechanism allowing member states to confiscate and sell Russian oil carried aboard shadow fleet vessels attempting to evade the bloc’s sanctions. title: Russia Forced to Import Gasoline From India Amid Domestic Shortages
text: Russia Forced to Import Gasoline From India Amid Domestic Shortages Aug. 12, 2026 Smoke rising above an oil refinery in Moscow following a Ukrainian strike. Social media via REUTERS Russia last week received its first shipment of gasoline from India to offset domestic fuel shortages caused by Ukrainian drone strikes on its oil refineries, Bloomberg reported Wednesday, citing ship tracking data. According to market analytics firm Kpler, the Indian gasoline arrived at a Russian port on Wednesday, Aug. 5. It was reportedly produced by Nayara Energy, an Indian refiner partially owned by Russian state oil giant Rosneft. Russian-flagged tanker Cyclone in mid-June reportedly loaded 42,000 metric tons of gasoline from the Vadinar refinery in western India and used a chain of shadow fleet tankers off the coast of Egypt. Last month, Reuters reported that Russia had quietly begun purchasing gasoline from Indian refineries to stabilize domestic supplies. Russian officials have since claimed the domestic fuel market partially stabilized. title: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App
text: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App Aug. 12, 2026 pay.yandex.ru Major Russian digital wallet and payment service Yandex Pay said Wednesday that its application had been removed from Apple’s App Store. The removal means iPhone users in Russia can no longer download or update Yandex Pay. The app allows users to store cards, make contactless payments and split purchases across Yandex’s suite of services. In a statement, Yandex Pay assured customers that their money remained secure and that the app would continue to function for users who already had it installed. “Most importantly, don’t delete the app,” Yandex Pay said, urging users to turn off automatic updates and use its web-based version within mobile browsers instead. “We’re sad this happened too… We’ll figure something out with the app,” Yandex Pay said. Apple has not publicly commented on the removal, though it has delisted apps linked to sanctioned Russian entities in recent months. While Yandex Pay has not itself been targeted directly by Western sanctions, Yandex Bank was sanctioned by the United Kingdom in June. Yandex Pay is still available for Android users on Google Play. text: Tyumen Region Imposes Mass Pig Culls Over Mystery Outbreak Aug. 12, 2026 72.ru Authorities in western Siberia’s Tyumen region have begun forcibly seizing and culling domestic pigs across several rural villages following an outbreak of an undisclosed disease, the local outlet 72.ru reported Wednesday. As part of quarantine measures imposed Friday, disinfection checkpoints manned by police have reportedly been set up along Golyshmanovsky District roads to spray passing vehicles and prevent pork products from leaving the area. Video shared by the outlet showed men in hazmat suits spraying vehicles and photographs of them inspecting pigsties. Alexander Khotin was detained Tuesday in the town of Mozhaysk west of Moscow, where they allegedly found a blood-stained knife inside a bathroom, according to RBC. Investigators launched a murder investigation. Telegram channels with links to Russia’s security services reported that, on Monday night, Khotin got into an argument with 54-year-old Alexander Kumantsov inside an apartment in western Moscow. Telegram channels Mash and Shot, however, disagree on Khotin’s age, with one writing he is 33, and the other 34 years old. During the altercation, Khotin allegedly stabbed Kumantsov at least seven times in the neck, face and head. title: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App
text: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App Aug. 12, 2026 pay.yandex.ru Major Russian digital wallet and payment service Yandex Pay said Wednesday that its application had been removed from Apple’s App Store. The removal means iPhone users in Russia can no longer download or update Yandex Pay. The app allows users to store cards, make contactless payments and split purchases across Yandex’s suite of services. In a statement, Yandex Pay assured customers that their money remained secure and that the app would continue to function for users who already had it installed. “Most importantly, don’t delete the app,” Yandex Pay said, urging users to turn off automatic updates and use its web-based version within mobile browsers instead. “We’re sad this happened too… We’ll figure something out with the app,” Yandex Pay said. Apple has not publicly commented on the removal, though it has delisted apps linked to sanctioned Russian entities in recent months. While Yandex Pay has not itself been targeted directly by Western sanctions, Yandex Bank was sanctioned by the United Kingdom in June. Yandex Pay is still available for Android users on Google Play. The removal means iPhone users in Russia can no longer download or update Yandex Pay. The app allows users to store cards, make contactless payments and split purchases across Yandex’s suite of services. In a statement, Yandex Pay assured customers that their money remained secure and that the app would continue to function for users who already had it installed. “Most importantly, don’t delete the app,” Yandex Pay said, urging users to turn off automatic updates and use its web-based version within mobile browsers instead. “We’re sad this happened too… We’ll figure something out with the app,” Yandex Pay said. Apple has not publicly commented on the removal, though it has delisted apps linked to sanctioned Russian entities in recent months. While Yandex Pay has not itself been targeted directly by Western sanctions, Yandex Bank was sanctioned by the United Kingdom in June. Yandex Pay is still available for Android users on Google Play. As part of quarantine measures imposed Friday, disinfection checkpoints manned by police have reportedly been set up along Golyshmanovsky District roads to spray passing vehicles and prevent pork products from leaving the area. Video shared by the outlet showed men in hazmat suits spraying vehicles and photographs of them inspecting pigsties. title: Orenburg Region Imposes Fuel Rationing After Ukrainian Refinery Attack
text: Orenburg Region Imposes Fuel Rationing After Ukrainian Refinery Attack Aug. 12, 2026 Ural56.ru Russia’s Orenburg region near the border with Kazakhstan has introduced fuel rationing and an odd-even license plate system at gas stations, following a Ukrainian drone attack on a local oil refinery. “I’ll be honest, our region is facing a difficult fuel situation. The enemy’s latest terrorist act has created certain problems,” Orenburg region Governor Yevgeny Solntsev said Wednesday. The Ukrainian military said Tuesday it had attacked the Orsknefteorgsintez refinery, located around 1,500 kilometers (930 miles) from the border with Ukraine. The refinery has an annual processing capacity of 6.6 million metric tons. Under the new restrictions, drivers with license plates ending in even numbers are limited to fuel purchases on even days, while those with license plates ending in odd numbers are limited to fuel purchases on odd days. Authorities have also capped individual fuel purchases at 30 liters (8 gallons) of gasoline per customer and banned sales into portable containers. title: Putin Threatens Retaliation if Europe Seizes Russian Ships
text: Putin Threatens Retaliation if Europe Seizes Russian Ships Aug. 12, 2026 President Vladimir Putin visits the Russian Navy missile cruiser Varyag. kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin said Moscow would retaliate in kind if European countries carried out plans to seize Russian commercial vessels, describing the proposed measures as “piracy and robbery.” “We see the authorities of certain countries attempting, in violation of international maritime law, to restrict the movement of vessels operated by our businesses,” Putin said during a meeting with Pacific Fleet personnel aboard the missile cruiser Varyag on Wednesday. “And recently, they went so far as to consider seizing our vessels and selling the property they have plundered from us. This is, of course, nothing other than piracy and robbery.” The warning follows the European Union’s adoption in July of a mechanism allowing member states to confiscate and sell Russian oil carried aboard shadow fleet vessels attempting to evade the bloc’s sanctions. title: Russia Forced to Import Gasoline From India Amid Domestic Shortages
text: Russia Forced to Import Gasoline From India Amid Domestic Shortages Aug. 12, 2026 Smoke rising above an oil refinery in Moscow following a Ukrainian strike. Social media via REUTERS Russia last week received its first shipment of gasoline from India to offset domestic fuel shortages caused by Ukrainian drone strikes on its oil refineries, Bloomberg reported Wednesday, citing ship tracking data. According to market analytics firm Kpler, the Indian gasoline arrived at a Russian port on Wednesday, Aug. 5. It was reportedly produced by Nayara Energy, an Indian refiner partially owned by Russian state oil giant Rosneft. Russian-flagged tanker Cyclone in mid-June reportedly loaded 42,000 metric tons of gasoline from the Vadinar refinery in western India and used a chain of shadow fleet tankers off the coast of Egypt. Last month, Reuters reported that Russia had quietly begun purchasing gasoline from Indian refineries to stabilize domestic supplies. Russian officials have since claimed the domestic fuel market partially stabilized. title: Orenburg Region Imposes Fuel Rationing After Ukrainian Refinery Attack
text: Orenburg Region Imposes Fuel Rationing After Ukrainian Refinery Attack Aug. 12, 2026 Ural56.ru Russia’s Orenburg region near the border with Kazakhstan has introduced fuel rationing and an odd-even license plate system at gas stations, following a Ukrainian drone attack on a local oil refinery. “I’ll be honest, our region is facing a difficult fuel situation. The enemy’s latest terrorist act has created certain problems,” Orenburg region Governor Yevgeny Solntsev said Wednesday. The Ukrainian military said Tuesday it had attacked the Orsknefteorgsintez refinery, located around 1,500 kilometers (930 miles) from the border with Ukraine. The refinery has an annual processing capacity of 6.6 million metric tons. Under the new restrictions, drivers with license plates ending in even numbers are limited to fuel purchases on even days, while those with license plates ending in odd numbers are limited to fuel purchases on odd days. Authorities have also capped individual fuel purchases at 30 liters (8 gallons) of gasoline per customer and banned sales into portable containers. title: Putin Threatens Retaliation if Europe Seizes Russian Ships
text: Putin Threatens Retaliation if Europe Seizes Russian Ships Aug. 12, 2026 President Vladimir Putin visits the Russian Navy missile cruiser Varyag. kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin said Moscow would retaliate in kind if European countries carried out plans to seize Russian commercial vessels, describing the proposed measures as “piracy and robbery.” “We see the authorities of certain countries attempting, in violation of international maritime law, to restrict the movement of vessels operated by our businesses,” Putin said during a meeting with Pacific Fleet personnel aboard the missile cruiser Varyag on Wednesday. “And recently, they went so far as to consider seizing our vessels and selling the property they have plundered from us. This is, of course, nothing other than piracy and robbery.” The warning follows the European Union’s adoption in July of a mechanism allowing member states to confiscate and sell Russian oil carried aboard shadow fleet vessels attempting to evade the bloc’s sanctions. title: Russia Forced to Import Gasoline From India Amid Domestic Shortages
text: Russia Forced to Import Gasoline From India Amid Domestic Shortages Aug. 12, 2026 Smoke rising above an oil refinery in Moscow following a Ukrainian strike. Social media via REUTERS Russia last week received its first shipment of gasoline from India to offset domestic fuel shortages caused by Ukrainian drone strikes on its oil refineries, Bloomberg reported Wednesday, citing ship tracking data. According to market analytics firm Kpler, the Indian gasoline arrived at a Russian port on Wednesday, Aug. 5. It was reportedly produced by Nayara Energy, an Indian refiner partially owned by Russian state oil giant Rosneft. Russian-flagged tanker Cyclone in mid-June reportedly loaded 42,000 metric tons of gasoline from the Vadinar refinery in western India and used a chain of shadow fleet tankers off the coast of Egypt. Last month, Reuters reported that Russia had quietly begun purchasing gasoline from Indian refineries to stabilize domestic supplies. Russian officials have since claimed the domestic fuel market partially stabilized. title: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App
text: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App Aug. 12, 2026 pay.yandex.ru Major Russian digital wallet and payment service Yandex Pay said Wednesday that its application had been removed from Apple’s App Store. The removal means iPhone users in Russia can no longer download or update Yandex Pay. The app allows users to store cards, make contactless payments and split purchases across Yandex’s suite of services. In a statement, Yandex Pay assured customers that their money remained secure and that the app would continue to function for users who already had it installed. “Most importantly, don’t delete the app,” Yandex Pay said, urging users to turn off automatic updates and use its web-based version within mobile browsers instead. “We’re sad this happened too… We’ll figure something out with the app,” Yandex Pay said. Apple has not publicly commented on the removal, though it has delisted apps linked to sanctioned Russian entities in recent months. While Yandex Pay has not itself been targeted directly by Western sanctions, Yandex Bank was sanctioned by the United Kingdom in June. Yandex Pay is still available for Android users on Google Play. text: Russia Forced to Import Gasoline From India Amid Domestic Shortages Aug. 12, 2026 Smoke rising above an oil refinery in Moscow following a Ukrainian strike. Social media via REUTERS Russia last week received its first shipment of gasoline from India to offset domestic fuel shortages caused by Ukrainian drone strikes on its oil refineries, Bloomberg reported Wednesday, citing ship tracking data. According to market analytics firm Kpler, the Indian gasoline arrived at a Russian port on Wednesday, Aug. 5. It was reportedly produced by Nayara Energy, an Indian refiner partially owned by Russian state oil giant Rosneft. Russian-flagged tanker Cyclone in mid-June reportedly loaded 42,000 metric tons of gasoline from the Vadinar refinery in western India and used a chain of shadow fleet tankers off the coast of Egypt. title: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App
text: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App Aug. 12, 2026 pay.yandex.ru Major Russian digital wallet and payment service Yandex Pay said Wednesday that its application had been removed from Apple’s App Store. The removal means iPhone users in Russia can no longer download or update Yandex Pay. The app allows users to store cards, make contactless payments and split purchases across Yandex’s suite of services. In a statement, Yandex Pay assured customers that their money remained secure and that the app would continue to function for users who already had it installed. “Most importantly, don’t delete the app,” Yandex Pay said, urging users to turn off automatic updates and use its web-based version within mobile browsers instead. “We’re sad this happened too… We’ll figure something out with the app,” Yandex Pay said. Apple has not publicly commented on the removal, though it has delisted apps linked to sanctioned Russian entities in recent months. While Yandex Pay has not itself been targeted directly by Western sanctions, Yandex Bank was sanctioned by the United Kingdom in June. Yandex Pay is still available for Android users on Google Play. title: Orenburg Region Imposes Fuel Rationing After Ukrainian Refinery Attack
text: Orenburg Region Imposes Fuel Rationing After Ukrainian Refinery Attack Aug. 12, 2026 Ural56.ru Russia’s Orenburg region near the border with Kazakhstan has introduced fuel rationing and an odd-even license plate system at gas stations, following a Ukrainian drone attack on a local oil refinery. “I’ll be honest, our region is facing a difficult fuel situation. The enemy’s latest terrorist act has created certain problems,” Orenburg region Governor Yevgeny Solntsev said Wednesday. The Ukrainian military said Tuesday it had attacked the Orsknefteorgsintez refinery, located around 1,500 kilometers (930 miles) from the border with Ukraine. The refinery has an annual processing capacity of 6.6 million metric tons. Under the new restrictions, drivers with license plates ending in even numbers are limited to fuel purchases on even days, while those with license plates ending in odd numbers are limited to fuel purchases on odd days. Authorities have also capped individual fuel purchases at 30 liters (8 gallons) of gasoline per customer and banned sales into portable containers. title: Putin Threatens Retaliation if Europe Seizes Russian Ships
text: Putin Threatens Retaliation if Europe Seizes Russian Ships Aug. 12, 2026 President Vladimir Putin visits the Russian Navy missile cruiser Varyag. kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin said Moscow would retaliate in kind if European countries carried out plans to seize Russian commercial vessels, describing the proposed measures as “piracy and robbery.” “We see the authorities of certain countries attempting, in violation of international maritime law, to restrict the movement of vessels operated by our businesses,” Putin said during a meeting with Pacific Fleet personnel aboard the missile cruiser Varyag on Wednesday. “And recently, they went so far as to consider seizing our vessels and selling the property they have plundered from us. This is, of course, nothing other than piracy and robbery.” The warning follows the European Union’s adoption in July of a mechanism allowing member states to confiscate and sell Russian oil carried aboard shadow fleet vessels attempting to evade the bloc’s sanctions. title: Russia Forced to Import Gasoline From India Amid Domestic Shortages
text: Russia Forced to Import Gasoline From India Amid Domestic Shortages Aug. 12, 2026 Smoke rising above an oil refinery in Moscow following a Ukrainian strike. Social media via REUTERS Russia last week received its first shipment of gasoline from India to offset domestic fuel shortages caused by Ukrainian drone strikes on its oil refineries, Bloomberg reported Wednesday, citing ship tracking data. According to market analytics firm Kpler, the Indian gasoline arrived at a Russian port on Wednesday, Aug. 5. It was reportedly produced by Nayara Energy, an Indian refiner partially owned by Russian state oil giant Rosneft. Russian-flagged tanker Cyclone in mid-June reportedly loaded 42,000 metric tons of gasoline from the Vadinar refinery in western India and used a chain of shadow fleet tankers off the coast of Egypt. Last month, Reuters reported that Russia had quietly begun purchasing gasoline from Indian refineries to stabilize domestic supplies. Russian officials have since claimed the domestic fuel market partially stabilized. title: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App
text: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App Aug. 12, 2026 pay.yandex.ru Major Russian digital wallet and payment service Yandex Pay said Wednesday that its application had been removed from Apple’s App Store. The removal means iPhone users in Russia can no longer download or update Yandex Pay. The app allows users to store cards, make contactless payments and split purchases across Yandex’s suite of services. In a statement, Yandex Pay assured customers that their money remained secure and that the app would continue to function for users who already had it installed. “Most importantly, don’t delete the app,” Yandex Pay said, urging users to turn off automatic updates and use its web-based version within mobile browsers instead. “We’re sad this happened too… We’ll figure something out with the app,” Yandex Pay said. Apple has not publicly commented on the removal, though it has delisted apps linked to sanctioned Russian entities in recent months. While Yandex Pay has not itself been targeted directly by Western sanctions, Yandex Bank was sanctioned by the United Kingdom in June. Yandex Pay is still available for Android users on Google Play. title: Tyumen Region Imposes Mass Pig Culls Over Mystery Outbreak
text: Tyumen Region Imposes Mass Pig Culls Over Mystery Outbreak Aug. 12, 2026 72.ru Authorities in western Siberia’s Tyumen region have begun forcibly seizing and culling domestic pigs across several rural villages following an outbreak of an undisclosed disease, the local outlet 72.ru reported Wednesday. As part of quarantine measures imposed Friday, disinfection checkpoints manned by police have reportedly been set up along Golyshmanovsky District roads to spray passing vehicles and prevent pork products from leaving the area. Video shared by the outlet showed men in hazmat suits spraying vehicles and photographs of them inspecting pigsties. Local veterinary officials reportedly refused to name the pathogen publicly, saying access to the information is restricted, while residents claimed it is being referred to as an “extraordinarily dangerous disease.” According to 72.ru, local agricultural experts believe the outbreak is likely African swine fever, a viral disease with a nearly 100% mortality rate among pigs but harmless to humans. title: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App
text: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App Aug. 12, 2026 pay.yandex.ru Major Russian digital wallet and payment service Yandex Pay said Wednesday that its application had been removed from Apple’s App Store. The removal means iPhone users in Russia can no longer download or update Yandex Pay. The app allows users to store cards, make contactless payments and split purchases across Yandex’s suite of services. In a statement, Yandex Pay assured customers that their money remained secure and that the app would continue to function for users who already had it installed. “Most importantly, don’t delete the app,” Yandex Pay said, urging users to turn off automatic updates and use its web-based version within mobile browsers instead. “We’re sad this happened too… We’ll figure something out with the app,” Yandex Pay said. Apple has not publicly commented on the removal, though it has delisted apps linked to sanctioned Russian entities in recent months. While Yandex Pay has not itself been targeted directly by Western sanctions, Yandex Bank was sanctioned by the United Kingdom in June. Yandex Pay is still available for Android users on Google Play. title: Orenburg Region Imposes Fuel Rationing After Ukrainian Refinery Attack
text: Orenburg Region Imposes Fuel Rationing After Ukrainian Refinery Attack Aug. 12, 2026 Ural56.ru Russia’s Orenburg region near the border with Kazakhstan has introduced fuel rationing and an odd-even license plate system at gas stations, following a Ukrainian drone attack on a local oil refinery. “I’ll be honest, our region is facing a difficult fuel situation. The enemy’s latest terrorist act has created certain problems,” Orenburg region Governor Yevgeny Solntsev said Wednesday. The Ukrainian military said Tuesday it had attacked the Orsknefteorgsintez refinery, located around 1,500 kilometers (930 miles) from the border with Ukraine. The refinery has an annual processing capacity of 6.6 million metric tons. Under the new restrictions, drivers with license plates ending in even numbers are limited to fuel purchases on even days, while those with license plates ending in odd numbers are limited to fuel purchases on odd days. Authorities have also capped individual fuel purchases at 30 liters (8 gallons) of gasoline per customer and banned sales into portable containers. title: Putin Threatens Retaliation if Europe Seizes Russian Ships
text: Putin Threatens Retaliation if Europe Seizes Russian Ships Aug. 12, 2026 President Vladimir Putin visits the Russian Navy missile cruiser Varyag. kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin said Moscow would retaliate in kind if European countries carried out plans to seize Russian commercial vessels, describing the proposed measures as “piracy and robbery.” “We see the authorities of certain countries attempting, in violation of international maritime law, to restrict the movement of vessels operated by our businesses,” Putin said during a meeting with Pacific Fleet personnel aboard the missile cruiser Varyag on Wednesday. “And recently, they went so far as to consider seizing our vessels and selling the property they have plundered from us. This is, of course, nothing other than piracy and robbery.” The warning follows the European Union’s adoption in July of a mechanism allowing member states to confiscate and sell Russian oil carried aboard shadow fleet vessels attempting to evade the bloc’s sanctions. text: Putin Threatens Retaliation if Europe Seizes Russian Ships Aug. 12, 2026 President Vladimir Putin visits the Russian Navy missile cruiser Varyag. kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin said Moscow would retaliate in kind if European countries carried out plans to seize Russian commercial vessels, describing the proposed measures as “piracy and robbery.” “We see the authorities of certain countries attempting, in violation of international maritime law, to restrict the movement of vessels operated by our businesses,” Putin said during a meeting with Pacific Fleet personnel aboard the missile cruiser Varyag on Wednesday. “And recently, they went so far as to consider seizing our vessels and selling the property they have plundered from us. This is, of course, nothing other than piracy and robbery.” The warning follows the European Union’s adoption in July of a mechanism allowing member states to confiscate and sell Russian oil carried aboard shadow fleet vessels attempting to evade the bloc’s sanctions. title: Russia Forced to Import Gasoline From India Amid Domestic Shortages
text: Russia Forced to Import Gasoline From India Amid Domestic Shortages Aug. 12, 2026 Smoke rising above an oil refinery in Moscow following a Ukrainian strike. Social media via REUTERS Russia last week received its first shipment of gasoline from India to offset domestic fuel shortages caused by Ukrainian drone strikes on its oil refineries, Bloomberg reported Wednesday, citing ship tracking data. According to market analytics firm Kpler, the Indian gasoline arrived at a Russian port on Wednesday, Aug. 5. It was reportedly produced by Nayara Energy, an Indian refiner partially owned by Russian state oil giant Rosneft. Russian-flagged tanker Cyclone in mid-June reportedly loaded 42,000 metric tons of gasoline from the Vadinar refinery in western India and used a chain of shadow fleet tankers off the coast of Egypt. Last month, Reuters reported that Russia had quietly begun purchasing gasoline from Indian refineries to stabilize domestic supplies. Russian officials have since claimed the domestic fuel market partially stabilized. title: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App
text: Apple Removes Yandex’s Payment Service App Aug. 12, 2026 pay.yandex.ru Major Russian digital wallet and payment service Yandex Pay said Wednesday that its application had been removed from Apple’s App Store. The removal means iPhone users in Russia can no longer download or update Yandex Pay. The app allows users to store cards, make contactless payments and split purchases across Yandex’s suite of services. In a statement, Yandex Pay assured customers that their money remained secure and that the app would continue to function for users who already had it installed. “Most importantly, don’t delete the app,” Yandex Pay said, urging users to turn off automatic updates and use its web-based version within mobile browsers instead. “We’re sad this happened too… We’ll figure something out with the app,” Yandex Pay said. Apple has not publicly commented on the removal, though it has delisted apps linked to sanctioned Russian entities in recent months. While Yandex Pay has not itself been targeted directly by Western sanctions, Yandex Bank was sanctioned by the United Kingdom in June. Yandex Pay is still available for Android users on Google Play.
